misconceptions.description: Designing the AI tutor to give the final answer on demand instead of holding a boundary that keeps the learner doing the thinking
misconceptions.trigger: learner specifies a tutor that solves the problem when asked rather than scaffolding the next step
misconceptions.feedback: A learning tutor's boundary is to support the learner's thinking, not replace it. Specify what the tutor will withhold (the final answer) and what it will offer (a next step or question).

misconceptions.description: Treating an AI-use disclosure as a generic blanket sentence rather than a specific account of which decision the AI touched
misconceptions.trigger: learner writes AI was used in this work without naming the bounded decision, the prompt, and what was accepted or rejected
misconceptions.feedback: A useful disclosure names the specific bounded decision the AI informed, what it proposed, and what you accepted or rejected. A blanket sentence is not auditable.

misconceptions.description: Assuming a confident, fluent tutor response is accurate and pedagogically appropriate without checking it against course evidence
misconceptions.trigger: learner accepts a tutor explanation because it sounds authoritative, with no verification step in the design
misconceptions.feedback: Fluency is not accuracy. Build a verification boundary so the tutor's output is checked against course material before a learner relies on it.
